_meta.description: Per-engagement lifestyle-attribute override for the creator_launch_demo engagement. Target audience: JasonTheWeen's audience — young Twitch/YouTube viewers of IRL/Just Chatting and gaming (Valorant) content, ages 18-26, low-to-moderate income, ~66% male / ~32% female, extremely online and creator/community-driven. Distributions retuned from US-general-adult priors to reflect this specific audience.
_meta.sources: Priors reflect an online-native, creator-fandom audience: very heavy social/creator media influence, online-first shopping, community-drop / impulse purchasing, early-adopter tilt, and — unlike a competitive-gamer or fitness audience — a LOWER share of fitness/performance orientation (this is a variety/IRL audience, not a training audience). Directional, not measured.
notes: Weights are relative and will be normalized. They don't need to sum to 1.

Conditional overrides (age/income) from the base file are intentionally REMOVED. The whole file is scoped to a single 18-26 audience, so age/income branching is redundant — the base weights below already reflect the target.
Attributes are the same 6 dimensions as the base file — this is a weight retune, not a taxonomy change.

Deliberate design choice: fitness/performance orientation is kept LOW (0.20). This audience follows Jason for IRL/variety/gaming entertainment, not training. This is why a recovery-collagen concept is expected to under-index — the panel should reflect that honestly rather than inflate supplement appeal.

Known limitation: primary_shopping_channel is a grocery-CPG taxonomy that doesn't cleanly fit creator merch / DTC drops. 'Primarily online' is used as the best proxy for the Shopify-drop / Amazon pattern typical of this audience.

shopping_mindset.description: Primary decision-making style when evaluating purchases.

health_orientation.description: How much health and wellness factor into purchase decisions.

brand_adoption_style.description: How open someone is to trying new products and brands.

primary_shopping_channel.description: Where this person does most of their shopping. (Note: base taxonomy is grocery-focused; 'primarily online' is the best proxy for the Shopify-drop / Amazon / DTC pattern typical of creator-merch buyers in this audience.)

media_influence.description: How this person discovers and evaluates new products.

persona_narrative_prompt.description: System prompt for the LLM call that generates a rich persona narrative from structured attributes.
persona_narrative_prompt.template:
You are a creative writer helping build realistic consumer research personas. Given the following demographic and lifestyle attributes, write a 2-3 paragraph first-person persona description. The persona should feel like a real, specific individual — not a marketing segment summary.

Rules:
- Write in third person ("They are..." not "I am...")
- Include specific but plausible details that bring the persona to life (e.g., specific routines, preferences, habits)
- Stay consistent with ALL provided attributes — don't contradict any of them
- Do NOT mention purchase intent or any specific product
- Do NOT include opinions about hypothetical products
- Focus on daily life, routines, values, and how they approach shopping decisions
- Keep it grounded and realistic — avoid caricature
- End with a brief note on what matters most to them when evaluating new products
